title: Sweden Names 26-Man World Cup Squad — Gyökeres and Isak Lead Potter's Group F Panel; Bardghji and Kulusevski Out
detail: Sweden head coach Graham Potter named his final 26-man squad for the 2026 World Cup on May 12, one of the first nations to confirm its definitive roster ahead of the June 2 FIFA publication date. Viktor Gyökeres (Arsenal) leads the attacking line after a prolific club season, joined by Alexander Isak (Liverpool) despite earlier fitness doubts during the spring. Anthony Elanga is also included among the forwards. Victor Lindelöf (Manchester United), one of Sweden's most capped players with 75 international appearances, captains the side. Notable omissions: Roony Bardghji (Barcelona), the 19-year-old prodigy regarded as one of Europe's most exciting young talents, was not selected — a decision that generated immediate debate in Swedish football. Dejan Kulusevski (Tottenham Hotspur) was left out due to injury, the tournament having arrived too soon after his layoff. Sweden are in Group F and face Tunisia at Estadio BBVA in Monterrey (June 14), the Netherlands at NRG Stadium in Houston (June 20), and Japan at AT&T Stadium in Dallas (June 25). Sweden qualified for 2026 by defeating Poland 3–0 in the UEFA Path B final at Friends Arena on March 31.

title: Mexico Scraps Plan to Shorten School Year for World Cup After Public Backlash
detail: Mexico's education authorities announced on May 12 that they were abandoning a proposal to shorten the 2025–2026 school year to allow students and families to follow the FIFA World Cup 2026, after the plan drew significant public criticism. Al Jazeera reported that the proposal had generated backlash from educators and parents who objected to restructuring the academic calendar around a sporting event. The reversal reflects the delicate balance Mexican authorities are navigating as hosts of three tournament venues — Estadio Azteca (Mexico City), Estadio Akron (Guadalajara), and Estadio BBVA (Monterrey) — while managing domestic expectations and public services. Mexico opens the entire tournament with the first match at Estadio Azteca on June 11 (vs. South Africa, Group A), giving Mexico's World Cup co-hosting role particular symbolic weight. The abandoned school-year plan follows the broader pattern of host nations adjusting civil life around the tournament.

media.caption: Mexico cancels school-year shortening plan after public backlash — 30 days before the June 11 World Cup opener at Estadio Azteca
